chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:

Indeed, God -- blessed and exalted be He -- established brotherhood between me and Ali ibn Abi Talib, and married him to my daughter from above His seven heavens, and made His angels of proximity bear witness to that, and made him my deputy and vicegerent. Ali is from me and I am from him; one who loves him loves me, and one who hates him hates me. And indeed the angels seek closeness to God through loving him.

key_terms.آخى: Established brotherhood (mu'akhat) -- refers to the pact of brotherhood the Prophet made between himself and Ali
key_terms.خليفة: Vicegerent/successor (khalifah) -- one who succeeds the Prophet in leadership
key_terms.وصيا: Deputy/executor (wasi) -- one entrusted with carrying out the Prophet's mission after him

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ali ibn Abi Talib on the Day of Ghadir?
ai.summary: In this hadith delivered on the Day of Ghadir Khumm -- a pivotal moment in Islamic history when the Prophet publicly declared Ali's authority -- the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) enumerates five divine honors bestowed upon Ali ibn Abi Talib: the establishment of brotherhood, the heavenly marriage to Fatimah al-Zahra, angelic witness, appointment as deputy and vicegerent, and the inseparability of their spiritual statuses. The hadith concludes with the powerful statement that even the angels seek proximity to God through loving Ali, underscoring the cosmic significance of wilayah in Shia theology.
